newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank fine-tunes baht remittance ban.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank fine-tunes baht remittance ban.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday said it had fine-tuned its temporary ban on foreign repatriation of baht funds derived from stock sales.
The move was seen as a bid to plug loopholes for currency speculators to obtain the local currency.
A central bank circular said foreign investors can keep proceeds from selling Thai stocks in their specific non-resident baht accounts opened with Thai banks or reinvest the funds in local equities.
It said the investors could not transfer the funds to other non-resident baht accounts. They would be allowed to repatriate the baht only in foreign currencies.
The bank said bona fide foreign investors could continue trading Thai stocks.
But bank custodians in Thailand were not permitted to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks among foreigners unless the transfers were backed by documentary evidence of transaction payment.

The circular, signed by Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, head of the central bank's financial institutions' supervision department, said the restrictions on both unpaid stock lendings and baht remittances took effect from Wednesday.

The central bank said to help the authorities monitor baht supply movement in non-resident baht accounts, foreign investors may need to maintain separate bank accounts so that stock sale proceeds could be separated from deposits from other sources.
